_description: Per-page-family <title> contract, derived from what's ACTUALLY implemented and tested against real data - not the illustrative templates in the task brief, which do not match any of the three real title formats already in production. All three real formats are kept as-is (each is deliberate, tested, and free of duplicates on its own dataset); this file documents them as the contract going forward rather than replacing them with one forced template.
globalNote: Brand suffix is NOT applied uniformly on purpose. Static pages and calculators append ' - Ali Demirbaş' (10-45 low-volume pages, brand repetition in SERPs is fine at that scale). The 211-page A/B test library and 255-page journey library deliberately do NOT append the person's name - see rejectedNaiveTemplate below for why forcing it there would be a real defect, not an improvement.

ab-test-library-detail.purpose: One A/B test scenario's own page - the search-facing rewrite of a Turkish internal question/hypothesis pair
ab-test-library-detail.primaryKeywordSource: src/data/ab-tests.json record's own `seoTitle` field (211/211 populated, English, editorially authored)
ab-test-library-detail.entitySource: the record's `question` (English seoTitle is a rewrite of the Turkish question's intent, not a translation - e.g. AB-001 question 'CTA buton rengi dönüşümü etkiler mi?' -> seoTitle 'CTA Button Color A/B Test Example on the Cart Page')
ab-test-library-detail.fallback: r.question (Turkish) if seoTitle is ever null - never happens today (0/211), but the live code (AbTestRoutes.tsx) already has this fallback so a future new record without a seoTitle degrades gracefully instead of rendering undefined
ab-test-library-detail.duplicatePreventionRule: already validated: 0 exact duplicates, 1 near-duplicate pair at similarity>=0.8 (verified via production/validate-seo-metadata.mjs check 17, which passed - the one near pair is flagged needsSeoReview)
ab-test-library-detail.verdict: KEEP - already production-quality and independently validated by a 23-check validator (production/validate-seo-metadata.mjs). This round's contribution is confirming it, not rewriting it.
ab-test-library-detail.knownGap: H1 (r.question) is Turkish; seoTitle is English - see seo/hreflang-and-language-status.json. This is a title/H1 relationship issue, not a title-contract defect on its own.

journey-library-index.purpose: Catalog/browse page for the 255-journey canonical library

journey-library-detail.primaryKeywordSource: journey.name (unique across all 255, 0 duplicates, length 35-87 chars median 62, per production/journey-seo-contract.json's own audit)
journey-library-detail.entitySource: journey.id (a short code like ACQ-01, prefixed onto the title) + journey.name
journey-library-detail.suffixPrefix: " - Canonical Journey Library" / " - Canonical Journey Kütüphanesi" (a sub-brand suffix, not the person's own name)
journey-library-detail.fallback: n/a - journey.name exists and is complete on all 255 records (production/journey-seo-contract.json titleSource.status: COMPLETE)
journey-library-detail.duplicatePreventionRule: journey.name is already unique across all 255 (0 duplicates, verified in the pre-existing audit contract); the ID prefix adds a second layer of uniqueness even in the hypothetical case two names collided
journey-library-detail.currentLiveConstruction: `${detail.id} ${detail.name} - ${suffix}` (JourneyRoutes.tsx:38), e.g. for ACC-71: "ACC-71 Entitlement Qualification - Canonical Journey Library"
journey-library-detail.differsFromAuditedArtifact: production/journey-seo-metadata.json independently authored its own seoTitle per record WITHOUT the ID prefix (e.g. "Entitlement Qualification Lifecycle Journey Example" for the same ACC-71) - a genuinely different, also-valid construction that is NOT what's live. Not reconciled this round (would mean editing JourneyRoutes.tsx, out of scope) - flagged as a decision the content owner should make: keep the ID-prefixed live version (more scannable in a 255-page corpus, doubles as a de-facto uniqueness guarantee) or switch to the shorter authored version (reads more like a normal search result, matches the illustrative template style in the original task brief more closely). Recommendation: keep the ID-prefixed live version - it's already working, already unique, and the ID prefix is a genuine navigational aid across a 255-page library that a shorter title would lose.
journey-library-detail.verdict: KEEP the live construction as this round's stated contract

rejectedNaiveTemplates.note: The task brief's own suggested templates were tested against real data and rejected - kept here as a record of why, per the brief's own instruction to not accept them blindly.

calculator.reality: content.seo.seoTitle is a fully custom editorial string (e.g. "Email Delivery Rate Calculator", "Revenue per Recipient Calculator"), joined with " - Ali Demirbaş" (hyphen, not pipe). Forcing a colon+formula-fragment into every one of 43 titles would either truncate awkwardly or force artificial phrasing onto calculators whose formula doesn't compress into a title fragment cleanly (e.g. multi-step funnel analysis, confidence interval).

abTest.brief: {Test Question / Topic}: A/B Test Example | Ali Demirbaş
abTest.reality: Real seoTitle values read as normal English phrases, not question-colon constructions ("CTA Button Color A/B Test Example on the Cart Page", not "Does CTA button color affect conversion?: A/B Test Example"), and never carry a brand suffix at all - see families.ab-test-library-detail above for why that's deliberate at this page count.

journey.brief: {Journey Name}: Lifecycle Marketing Journey | Ali Demirbaş
journey.reality: Real live titles are "{ID} {Name} - Canonical Journey Library" (en dash, not colon; ID-prefixed; library-branded, not person-branded, and not literally "Lifecycle Marketing Journey"). The task brief's exact phrase never appears anywhere in the real data or the real rendering code.
